macos.rationale: Apple-silicon macOS app in the official first-task tutorial. Linux/Windows daemon access does not establish desktop builds.

windows.rationale: The complete first-party app inventory says the repository holds all clients and lists only macOS desktop shells plus web/daemon/CLI; it omits this native client. Remote daemon OS support is distinct.

linux.rationale: The complete first-party app inventory says the repository holds all clients and lists only macOS desktop shells plus web/daemon/CLI; it omits this native client. Remote daemon OS support is distinct.

web-client.rationale: Browser client can start, watch and message remote sessions; desktop-only tools retain their documented scope.

mobile-web.rationale: Phone browser can create, watch and message remote sessions. Native iOS/Android apps remain unknown.

ios.rationale: The complete first-party app inventory says the repository holds all clients and lists only macOS desktop shells plus web/daemon/CLI; it omits this native client. Remote daemon OS support is distinct.

android.rationale: The complete first-party app inventory says the repository holds all clients and lists only macOS desktop shells plus web/daemon/CLI; it omits this native client. Remote daemon OS support is distinct.

cli.rationale: Product-owned HumanLayer CLI proxies task/session API operations and runs automations; it is separate from coding-agent CLIs.

claude-code.rationale: Pinned current application README explicitly names Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi. Harness-specific plugins/auth apply; no cross-harness fixture was run.

codex.rationale: Pinned current application README explicitly names Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi. Harness-specific plugins/auth apply; no cross-harness fixture was run.

opencode.rationale: Pinned current application README explicitly names Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi. Harness-specific plugins/auth apply; no cross-harness fixture was run.

pi.rationale: Pinned current application README explicitly names Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi. Harness-specific plugins/auth apply; no cross-harness fixture was run.

cursor.rationale: The closed coding-agent schema and daemon launcher gate omit and reject this agent family; model gateways do not add a coding-harness route.

gemini-cli.rationale: The closed coding-agent schema and daemon launcher gate omit and reject this agent family; model gateways do not add a coding-harness route.

grok.rationale: The closed coding-agent schema and daemon launcher gate omit and reject this agent family; model gateways do not add a coding-harness route.

aider.rationale: The closed coding-agent schema and daemon launcher gate omit and reject this agent family; model gateways do not add a coding-harness route.

antigravity.rationale: The closed coding-agent schema and daemon launcher gate omit and reject this agent family; model gateways do not add a coding-harness route.

byo-subscription.rationale: The daemon signs in through the installed Claude Code CLI's own auth login and runs sessions on that installed executable; the pricing FAQ says existing Claude/Codex subscriptions can be used. Source-inspected; not tested. Scope: Current HumanLayer desktop and hosted UI.

local.rationale: Daemon executes on the workstation or a user-provided server/VM. User supplies and supervises compute; vendor-hosted UI is not managed agent compute.

own-server.rationale: Daemon executes on the workstation or a user-provided server/VM. User supplies and supervises compute; vendor-hosted UI is not managed agent compute.

worktree.rationale: Task branches and multi-repository worktrees separate code. No security sandbox or container/VM option is inferred.

container.rationale: The documentation explicitly supports running the agent daemon in a user-managed container with persisted credentials. This is a host-level option, not a product-created container per session.

vm.rationale: The documentation explicitly supports a user-provisioned VM daemon host, including suspension/persistence requirements. No per-session VM provisioning is claimed.

parallel-runs.rationale: Shipped release notes (0.149.0) describe agents running in parallel in the task/session lists; the product ships from main continuously. Not tested. Scope: Current HumanLayer desktop and hosted UI.

coordinator.rationale: Bundled HumanLayer orchestration skill drives product CLI task/session launches, status inspection and artifacts. This is a product-supplied skill, distinct from a tested cross-harness hierarchy.

unattended-triggers.rationale: CI/cron can invoke product automation run without an interactive start. Scheduler and concurrency controls run in the user-owned external workflow.

multiplayer.rationale: Release notes explicitly describe shared prompting/drafts with presence and queued message authors. No two-account ordering fixture was performed.

roles.rationale: Organization admin controls integrations; task editors can add sessions/edit files and reviewers comment. Full role/revocation enforcement remains untested.

sso.rationale: SSO/SAML is listed on the custom-priced Enterprise plan only. Configuration not observed. Scope: Current HumanLayer desktop and hosted UI.

pr-workflow.rationale: Opt-in GitHub tab and PR skills create/manage PRs and display review/check information. GitHub integration and experimental settings apply.

review-ui.rationale: Product diff view documents changed files and inline comments. Batch review efficiency and exact-revision authority remain unknown.

license.rationale: The pinned current application monorepo, including client/API/daemon, carries Apache-2.0; separately licensed vendored MIT folders are disclosed. This is not inferred from the old SDK.

self-hosting.rationale: The pinned README says Cloud runs this code, the devstack runs the whole stack locally and gives a Docker Compose starter for self-hosting; guides are in progress and no install was tested.

telemetry-opt-out.rationale: The source-build documentation explicitly keeps Sentry/PostHog disabled when their environment keys are unset. Scope is self-built clients; hosted-app defaults remain separate.

free-tier.rationale: Starter is a recurring free plan for up to three members and 200 sessions/month, and the macOS app is a free download; agent and compute costs stay separate. Scope: Current HumanLayer desktop and hosted UI.

starting-price.rationale: Current advertised recurring Starter ADE price is free, subject to three-member/200-session limits and the announced hosted transition. Pro is separately advertised at USD 100/user/month.

laptop-independent.rationale: A supervised reachable remote daemon performs execution while browser/phone clients connect independently. Closing the controlling laptop does not shut down that remote host.

free-plan.rationale: Starter free up to three members.

no-paid-plan.rationale: The complete public plan list includes paid Pro and Enterprise alongside Starter.

subscription.rationale: Pro has a recurring USD 100/user/month charge, with separate agent and own-compute costs.

usage-based.rationale: The complete first-party plan list offers recurring seat-priced Pro and custom Enterprise and omits consumption-meter, compute-meter and one-time ADE pricing; provider/host bills are separate.

compute.rationale: The complete first-party plan list offers recurring seat-priced Pro and custom Enterprise and omits consumption-meter, compute-meter and one-time ADE pricing; provider/host bills are separate.

one-time.rationale: The complete first-party plan list offers recurring seat-priced Pro and custom Enterprise and omits consumption-meter, compute-meter and one-time ADE pricing; provider/host bills are separate.

issue-tracking.rationale: Tasks are persistent, but the product's own CLI reference explicitly states a task has no status of its own (statuses belong to sessions); issue state lives in linked GitHub/Linear/Jira trackers. Scope: Current HumanLayer desktop and hosted UI.
